Load 12: little-endian update target $9249. The resident indirect jump at $0450, the last step of a main-loop pass, takes it while the game-exit flag $0840 is zero, the selected player's meter $4DCD,X is nonzero and the status $5284 that $7B84 returns is nonzero. Load 12: player frame byte $66. $6C4A stores it at $4A and stores the value minus $66 modulo 256 at $1177.

Load 12: the map's width in metatiles, $4C. The rightward-scroll check at $0EF7–$0F02 compares the metatile column just past the view's right edge with it and skips the scroll when that column is not smaller, and the entity rightward move at $4593 undoes a move whose next column equals it.
The downward-scroll check at $0CCC–$0CD9 compares the next map-row position with this value.

Load 12: the view origin, column $71 and row $0C in characters. The screen builder $6D17 halves them at $6D26 and $6D2B to find the first metatile to draw; $6D8B–$6DA0 copies them to the left and top view bounds and computes right and bottom by adding $25 and $12 modulo 256; $6DA3–$6DBE scrolls once more down or right for an odd row or column; and $6DC1–$6DD6 stores the final bounds, adding $26 and $13. $33EC–$3408 saves both bytes, puts the current view's left and top ($569B, $569D) there for $6D17 to redraw the screen, and restores them.
The little-endian address $A67F of this load’s entity records. $1863 copies it into the pointer at $E2–$E3.

The initial entity-slot limit is 4. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 4 ($18CB). The load has 8 entity records, so the initializer stops at the limit with records 5–8 left; each pass, the slot scan at $3622 checks slots 1 to 4 ($3629), and $3632 gives an empty slot the next record (counter $7C) or, once the zero byte after record 8 is reached, reloads the slot's own record at $366A.

A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and ($5A) at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

Load 12: low bytes for pointer entries 16–79 of the 81-entry split table. Paired with the high table, these encode $8E71 through $ADF1 in 128-byte steps modulo 65536, the row stride at $7F4A. They lie beyond the map’s 16 rows, the count at $7F4C. The window draw at $6D30 and the scroll readers at $2CD4, $2DC9, $2EC2 and $2F9D index by the view’s rows, which the scroll check at $0CCC keeps within the map. The hero’s tile checks index the table by his row $6F3D ($0EA7, $1041, $6E77) or that row plus one ($0C47, $0C69, $6E8D); $6F3D reaches 16 when the view is at the bottom of the map and the hero at his lowest screen position $E1 ($0CFC), so entries 16 and 17 can be read, and no hero check reaches entries 18–79. The entity collision checks at $451D and $4638 index the table by an entity’s tile row from $71DB, plus one to three, with no bound of their own.

Reached from the balance check when the gold covers stage field $4789,X. Test bit 0 of stage field $4753,X: clear selects message $9C90, set selects $9C79. Both jump to $9A29, which shows the message and starts the choice loop.

Save X in the immediate operand at $98D7 and Y in the one at $98D2, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $9BF0, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. A tens code of 1 is written as zero. Restore Y, call $9B97, restore X and return.

The flags come from the selection byte $9BF6, loaded at $9AC2 before the only jump here ($9AC5, taken when the layout gate $9BF5 is nonzero): negative ($FF, left) enters the first-price balance check at $990B; zero selects message $9CB7 at $9959; otherwise (1, right) take the second-price path at $98DD.

Reached from $98D9 when the shop selection byte is 1. Load X from $7B and call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, record byte 9, the second price: $78D1 subtracts it in packed decimal from the selected player’s gold and restores the gold if that borrows. Reload X and read callback high byte $4771,X. If nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $98FB from $476B/$4771 (record bytes 4 and 5), clear the high byte in the stage record so that the callback runs only once, and call the patched target; then use A=4 at $994E, which adds it to the life meter. If zero, enter the message path at $9902, which shows message $9D25 and then does the same with A=4. In load 12, stage record 1 at $927B names this shop’s entry $9846, with second price $05 and callback $928B.

Load 12: the operand of the JSR at $98FA, which the second-price path at $98DD fills before the call: once $78D1 has taken the second price $4789,X from the gold, $98EC stores the high byte from $4771,X and $98F2 the low byte from $476B,X, the record's bytes 5 and 4 (counting from 0), and $98F7 stores 0 in $4771,X. After the call, LDA #$04 and the JMP at $98FF go to $994E, which adds 4 to the meter through $77A9. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 1, which starts at $9333, also takes $98FB–$9901 to $D5C8–$D5CE as character $B9.

Second-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9D25 (“Nice and cold, / is'nt it?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=4 and jump to $9949, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 4 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $98EA branches here when the callback high byte $4771,X (record byte 5) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the second price, record byte 9, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. In load 12 stage-object record 1 at $927B names the price set-up $9846 as its callback.

Load 12: the start of the first-price balance check, which the BMI at $98D9 takes when the selection byte is $FF (left): load the selected player $4DBD into Y and the record index $7B into X, and read the high byte of the player's gold, $4DC7,Y. The BNE after it goes to the first-price purchase at $9920 when that byte is nonzero; otherwise $9915 compares the low byte $4DC9,Y with the first price $4783,X, and the JMP at $991D goes to $9A49 when the gold is lower. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 1, which starts at $9333, also takes $990B–$9912 to $D5D8–$D5DF as character $BB.

Reached from the balance check at $990B, which the selection path sends here when the shop selection byte is $FF and lets through when the selected player’s gold covers the first price. Call $78D1 with stage field $4783,X, record byte 8, the first price, which $78D1 subtracts in packed decimal from the gold, and reload the stage index. If callback high byte $477D,X is nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $993C from $4777/$477D (record bytes 6 and 7), clear that high byte so that the callback runs only once, and call the target; then use A=8 at $994E, which adds it to the life meter. Otherwise enter the message path at $9943, which shows message $9D40 and then does the same with A=8. In load 12, stage record 1 at $927B names this shop’s entry $9846, with first price $08 and callback $92DA.

Load 12: the first-price fallback, which the BEQ at $992B takes when the record's first-item callback high byte $477D,X is zero: load message pointer $9D40 in X/Y and A = 8, and fall into $9949, which shows the message through $77E0, and then $994E adds 8 to the meter through $77A9. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 1, which starts at $9333, also takes $9943–$9948 to $D610–$D615 as character $C2.

Push A, call $77E0 with the message pointer in X/Y and pull A, then continue at $994E, which adds A to the player’s meter through $77A9. The second-price fallback jumps here from $9908 with A=4 and message $9D25; the first-price fallback falls in from $9943 with A=8 and message $9D40.

Call $77A9 with A=4 or A=8, reload stage index, decrement $4753,X and jump to $9B39. The two price paths jump here, $98FF with A=4 and $9940 with A=8, after paying. $77A9 adds A to the selected player’s life meter $4DCD,Y, capped at the limit $4DCF,Y; $9B39 calls $3C2A and $370B until the message countdown $4D6B is zero and returns. In load 12 stage record $927B names this shop’s entry.
Load X/Y with message pointer $9CB7 and jump to the message call at $9B36. $98DB branches here when the selection byte read at $9AC2 is zero.

Reload stage index, decrement $4753,X, load message pointer $9D01 in X/Y and jump to the message call at $9B36. The only jump here is from the timeout path at $9A6E, taken when the layout gate $9BF5 is nonzero.
Store zero at the layout gate $9BF5, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and set $4D69 to 7. Reload stage index from $7B and continue to the item-pair selection at $997D. The jump entry at $9849 leads here.

Read $476B,X. If nonzero, pass it and $4771,X separately through the conditional-item resolver at $9B45; store the returned values at $9BFB/$9BFC, then jump to $99BA. If zero, branch to the implicit pair at $9996.

Use $4771,X, byte 5 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, as Y. Clear carry, add the selected player $4DBD (0 or 1) and then $D5, and store the sum as the low byte of the LDA at $99AA; store $4D plus the carry as its high byte. Load 12 never runs it: no stage-object record names the shop's item-pair entry at $9849, which leads here; record 1 at $927B names the price entry at $9846.

Read the absolute address patched by $99A0 and $99A7, $4DD5 plus stage field $4771,X plus the selected player index; clear carry and add $9BFD,Y, where Y is that stage field. Store the result at $9BFB, then store that result plus one modulo 256 at $9BFC. Continue at $99BA.

Load 12: the operand of the LDA at $99AA, which $99A0 and $99A7 set to $4DD5 plus the record's $4771,X plus the selected player $4DBD, so the LDA reads that player's byte there. The CLC and ADC $9BFD,Y after it add the offset for Y = $4771,X, STA $9BFB stores the sum as the first item, and CLC, ADC #$01 and STA $9BFC store the next item number as the second. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 1, which starts at $9333, also takes $99AB–$99B9 to $D678–$D686 as characters $CF–$D0.

Load the second item's number from $9BFC, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and read the picture-routine address at offsets 2 and 3 of its row in the 24-row item table at $9F4C. Patch the JSR operand at $99D0/$99D1. Load 12 never runs it: no stage-object record names the shop's item-pair entry at $9849; record 1 at $927B names the price entry at $9846.

Multiply A, the second item's number that $99BA loads from $9BFC, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9F4E,Y and $9F4F,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $99CF, which calls it with A=$E4. No stage record in load 12 names the item-shop entry $9849, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $996C, so this code does not run in load 12.
Call the patched target with A=$E4. Then read the first item byte at $9BFB, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and patch the JSR operand at $99E8/$99E9 from the same pointer table.

Multiply A, the first item's number that $99D2 loads from $9BFB, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9F4E,Y and $9F4F,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $99E7, which calls it with A=$D0. No stage record in load 12 names the item-shop entry $9849, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $996C, so this code does not run in load 12.
Call the second patched target with A=$D0, then set the temporary row counter at $9F4B to 3 and begin filling colour RAM.

For each of three rows, write colour 9 to four bytes at $D8F8,Y and four at $D90C,Y. Y starts at zero and advances by 40 after each row; the counter at $9F4B ends at zero. With I/O visible, these are colour RAM writes. The next setup continues at $9A09.

Load 12: the inner loop of the item-picture colour fill at $99F1: store colour 9 at $D8F8,Y and $D90C,Y. The INY, DEX and BPL after it repeat this four times a row, and $99FF adds 36 more to Y, 40 in all, for each of the three rows that $9F4B counts, so columns 8–11 and 28–31 of rows 6–8 take colour 9. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 1, which starts at $9333, also takes $99F3–$99FA to $D6C0–$D6C7 as character $D8.
Store $46 plus one modulo 256 at $9BAB. Pass the first selected item at $9BFB to $9BB2, then call $9B97 with Y=$73. Repeat for the second item at $9BFC with Y=$87.

Call $77E0 with the message pointer selected by the preceding path, then fall through to the mode and countdown initializer at $9A2C. The item-pair path loads $9C02; the price path jumps here from $98A5 or $98AC with $9C90 or $9C79.

Store 0 in the selection byte at $9BF6, store $DC in the countdown at $9BFA, and fall through to the wait path at $9A36. Besides this store, only the left and right handlers write the selection byte, and they keep it among $FF, 0 and 1.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $9BFA and branch to $9A69 when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9B6D and $9B5A; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $9A49. Starting from the initialized $DC, the countdown reaches zero on the 220th call to $3C2A, counting the calls of this loop and of the one at $9A49 together.
Call $3C2A, decrement $9BFA and branch to $9A69 at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9B6D and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $9A5A.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $9ABD; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $9A7F; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $9A9D. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $9A49. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.

Reached when the countdown at $9BFA reaches zero. If $9BF5 is nonzero, jump to $9960. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $9C37, and jump to the $77E0 call at $9B36.

If the signed mode byte at $9BF6 is negative, return to the wait path at $9A36. Otherwise decrement it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9BF5 is zero, pass the item index at $9BFB to the message selector at $9B85. Call $9B6D and return to the wait path.

If the mode byte at $9BF6 equals 1, return to the wait path at $9A36. Otherwise increment it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9BF5 is zero, pass the item index at $9BFC to the message selector at $9B85. Call $9B6D and return to the wait path.

Read the layout gate $9BF5; if nonzero, load the selection byte $9BF6 and jump to $98D9. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $9BF6. If nonzero, branch to the purchase index choice at $9AE6, preserving the negative flag from that read. If zero, inspect $4753,X: a negative value or a clear bit 1 selects message pointer $9C5F; a nonnegative value with bit 1 set selects $9C48. Both paths jump to the $77E0 message call. $9BF5 is $46 plus one on the price path ($9852) and zero on the item-pair path ($996E).
Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $9BFB when it is set, or $9BFC when clear, then enter the price selector at $9AF1. The path at $9ABD supplies that flag from $9BF6.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the item row's price at $9F4C,Y and $9F4D,Y (row offsets 0 and 1) to $7D/$7E. Call $7901, which subtracts the packed-decimal amount from the selected player’s gold, restores it on insufficient funds, returns carry set on success and clears decimal mode. The code at $9AE6 passes the first item's number from $9BFB when the selection byte is negative, or the second item's from $9BFC. No stage record in load 12 names the item-shop entry $9849, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $996C, so this code does not run in load 12.

After the $7901 price subtraction, jump to $9A36 on clear carry. On set carry, load X from $7B and decrement $4753,X with eight-bit wrap. Read $9BF6; if negative select the item index at $9BFB, otherwise select $9BFC. Push it and continue to the offset-4 routine-pointer selector at $9B1B.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's purchase-routine address at $9F50,Y and $9F51,Y (row offsets 4 and 5) into the operand of the JSR at $9B2F, which calls it with the item number plus 1 in A. A is the bought item's number, pushed by the code before: the first item from $9BFB when the selection byte is negative, otherwise the second from $9BFC. No stage record in load 12 names the item-shop entry $9849, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $996C, so this code does not run in load 12.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector. Load X/Y with $9C24 and call $77E0, then call $3C2A and $370B repeatedly while $4D6B is nonzero. Return once it is zero.
Load 12: return A unchanged unless it equals $13. For $13, inspect bit $10 of the selected player’s flags: return $14 when set, or $13 when clear. The shop item-pair path uses this resolver.

Load 12: call the input sampler at $3C4C and return carry set if any of $73, $74 or $70 is zero, carry clear if all are nonzero. The sampler reads joystick port 2 active-low, so carry is set while the stick is pushed left or right or fire is pressed.

Load 12: with decimal mode clear, add one to the selection byte at $9BF6, use the wrapped result as an index into $9BF7, and pass that position in X and $82 in Y to $719E. The selection byte stays among $FF, 0 and 1, so the index is 0 to 2.
Load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X and return. The insufficient-gold path calls it at $9890, and the item effects at $A00F, $A015, $A01B, $A021, $A02A, $A036 and $A053 tail-call it.

Multiply A, an item's number, by 8 using three eight-bit shifts, clear carry, add 6 and use the eight-bit result as X. Read the high byte from $9F4D,X into Y and the low byte from $9F4C,X into X, the message pointer at offsets 6 and 7 of the item's row in the 24-row item table at $9F4C, then jump to $77E0. Entry $77E0 loads A=0, so the message routine uses X/Y as a direct pointer. The selection paths call this routine at $9A94 with the first item's number from $9BFB and at $9AB4 with the second's from $9BFC. Load 12 never runs it: no stage-object record names the shop's item-pair entry at $9849; record 1 at $927B names the price entry at $9846.

Load 12: process four price-display bytes at $9BF0 in reverse order. Leave zero unchanged; add $F5 to each nonzero byte with eight-bit wrap and decimal mode clear. Call the digit writer at $9BA9 with successive Y positions, decrementing Y after each call.

Load 12: store A at offset Y of the page after $46, through STA $FF00,Y. $984F and $9A0C each set its high byte $9BAB to $46 plus one, $C1 or $C5, since $46 holds the screen page $C0 or $C4; the load holds $FF there. Then write colour 1 to $D900,Y, the matching colour RAM, and return. Called from $9BA1. Colour RAM requires I/O visible.

Load 12: multiply item ID A by eight with eight-bit wrap, split the two packed bytes from the item table at $9F4C into four nibble-plus-one values at $9BF0, and replace consecutive leading ones with zero. Nibbles and item indexes are not locally validated.

Load 12: four working price-display bytes. The item-price formatter at $9BB2 and the stage-price formatter at $98AF write them, and the drawing loop at $9B97 reads them in reverse, from $9BF3 down to $9BF0, passing each to the digit writer at $9BA9.

Load 12: one byte, $01 in the load, between the four price-display cells at $9BF0–$9BF3 and the layout gate at $9BF5. No instruction in load 12 or in the resident part names it, and the indexed accesses to $9BF0 at $9B99, $9BE0 and $9BE7 keep X between 0 and 3, so none reaches it.
Load 12: mutable shop layout gate. Timeout, selection and purchase code read this byte to choose alternate paths.
Load 12: mutable shop selection byte. The input loop initializes it to zero, left and right paths update it, and the cursor helper indexes the position table using this value plus one.

Load 12: three cursor-position bytes, $5F, $B4 and $FF, for selections $FF, 0 and 1: the cursor helper at $9B6D reads them at $9B76 with the selection byte plus one as index, and passes the byte in X to $719E. No instruction writes them.
Load 12: mutable shop timeout. The input loop initializes it to $DC and decrements it during both input-release and polling paths.

Load 12: mutable first item ID. $9987 or $99B1 stores it; the item drawing at $99D2, the price label at $9A0F, the left-selection description at $9A91 and the purchase paths at $9AEE and $9B17 read it.

Load 12: mutable second item ID. $9990 or $99B7 stores it; the item drawing at $99BA, the price label at $9A1A, the right-selection description at $9AB1 and the purchase paths at $9AE8 and $9B11 read it.

Load 12: five item-index offsets, $00, $00, $0D, $00 and $06, at $9BFD–$9C01. ADC $9BFD,Y at $99AE adds the selected offset to the player-state value and stores the first item ID; the following addition of one supplies the second ID, with Y equal to stage field $4771,X. Load 12 never reads them: its only stage record, record 1 at $927B, names the price entry $9846, and nothing names the item-pair entry $9849.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Welcome!” / “May I help you?” / “”, then the control byte $20. The instruction sequence at $9A25 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 32 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “Thank you.” / “”, then the control byte $10. The instruction sequence at $9B32 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 3: three zero-terminated fields "" / "      Closed." / "", followed by control byte $18. The shop timeout at $9A69, when the layout gate $9BF5 is zero, stores $FF in stage field $4753,X and loads this address in X/Y at $9A78, then jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 24 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 4: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10. The purchase gate at $9ABD loads this address in X/Y at $9ADF when the selection byte is zero and stage field $4753,X is not negative and has bit 1 set, then jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 5: three zero-terminated fields "Oh, he's" / "just browsing." / "", followed by control byte $10. The purchase gate at $9ABD loads this address in X/Y at $9AD4 when the selection byte is zero and stage field $4753,X is negative or has bit 1 clear, then jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 6: three zero-terminated fields "" / "  Cocktail or Beer." / "", followed by control byte $10. The sufficient-gold branch at $989A loads this address in X/Y at $98A8 when bit 0 of stage field $4753,X is set, then jumps to $9A29, which calls $77E0 and starts the choice loop. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 7: three zero-terminated fields "You're here again," / "Beer or Cocktail." / "", followed by control byte $10. The sufficient-gold branch at $989A loads this address in X/Y at $98A1 when bit 0 of stage field $4753,X is clear, then jumps to $9A29, which calls $77E0 and starts the choice loop. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 8: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10. The code at $9959, which the purchase path enters when the selection byte is zero, loads this address in X/Y and jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 9: three zero-terminated fields "" / "  Never come back!" / "", followed by control byte $10. The insufficient-gold branch at $988C, when stage field $4753,X is not 3 and has bit 0 set, calls $9B7D, which stores $FF in $4753,X, then loads this address in X/Y at $9893 and jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 10: three zero-terminated fields "Come back" / "with some money." / "", followed by control byte $10. The code at $9885, reached when stage field $4753,X is 3 or has bit 0 clear, loads this address in X/Y and jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 11: three zero-terminated fields "If you have no" / "business, Get out!" / "", followed by control byte $10. The shop timeout at $9A69, when the layout gate $9BF5 is nonzero, jumps to $9960, which decrements stage field $4753,X, loads this address in X/Y at $9965 and jumps to the $77E0 call at $9B36. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 12, shop message 12: three zero-terminated fields "Nice and cold," / "is'nt it?" / "", followed by control byte $10. The second-price fallback at $9902 loads this address in X/Y and A with 4 and jumps to $9949, which calls $77E0 and then $77A9 with A = 4. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “How do you like” / “the cocktail?” / “”, then the control byte $10. The instruction sequence at $9943 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “CLOTH BOOTS” / “”, then the control byte $10. Item row 0 of the shop table at $9F4C holds this address as its message pointer, at $9F52 (offset 6). When the shop cursor moves onto an item, $9A94 (the first item, $9BFB) or $9AB4 (the second, $9BFC) passes its row number to the message selector $9B85, which reads the pointer into X/Y and jumps to $77E0; that loads A with 0 and copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “LEATHER BOOTS” / “”, then the control byte $10. Item row 1 of the shop table at $9F4C holds this address as its message pointer, at $9F5A (offset 6). When the shop cursor moves onto an item, $9A94 (the first item, $9BFB) or $9AB4 (the second, $9BFC) passes its row number to the message selector $9B85, which reads the pointer into X/Y and jumps to $77E0; that loads A with 0 and copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.
